extracted.intended_audience: early-career cancer researchers applying for the Damon Runyon-Rachleff Innovation Award
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluation criteria for applicants seeking the Damon Runyon-Rachleff Innovation Award — a grant for early-career investigators proposing high-risk/high-reward cancer research that lacks preliminary data. Includes eligibility, funding use, reporting, and review standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant’s capacity for bold, exceptionally creative research
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant’s capacity to conduct bold, exceptionally creative research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications will be evaluated on the applicant’s demonstrated ability to carry out bold, highly creative research (evidence of creativity, prior accomplishments, independence). This is a central evaluation dimension used by the Innovation Award Committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty and creativity of proposed research (no incremental advances)
rubrics_metrics.description: The novelty and creativity of the proposed research. Incremental research will not be funded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposal must be novel and exceptionally creative. The program specifically funds innovative new ideas lacking preliminary data rather than incremental advances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential for significant impact on cancer prevention, diagnosis, treatment, or basic understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: The potential of the proposed research to lead to advances that will significantly impact the prevention, diagnosis, treatment or basic understanding of cancer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should articulate how success would translate into significant advances in the cancer field (clinical or basic science impact). For consideration for continued funding (years 3–4) the project must have potential to be transformative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant’s demonstrated need / lack of resources for proposed project
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant’s lack of resources to pursue the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award targets investigators who lack sufficient preliminary data or resources to obtain traditional funding; evidence of need strengthens competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-risk/high-reward focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for high-risk/high-reward ideas that could significantly impact cancer research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Award is designed to fund exceptionally creative, potentially transformative work that is sufficiently risky that conventional funders would likely not support it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early-career investigator status and category eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must belong to one of specified early-career categories (tenure-track assistant professors within first five years of initial position; clinical instructors/senior clinical fellows in final year of subspecialty training pursuing independent research; distinguished fellows with dedicated lab space).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cut-off example: tenure-track assistant professors within first five years of obtaining initial position (cut-off date noted). Joint submissions are allowed if both collaborators meet eligibility. Certain titles (ad hoc assistant professors, research assistant professors, research associate professors, instructors, research scientists and postdoctoral fellows) are not eligible. Contact awards@damonrunyon.org if unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. research institution and degree requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants (including non-U.S. citizens) must be conducting independent research at a U.S. research institution and must have received an MD, DO, PhD, or MD/PhD from an accredited institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic and translational/clinical projects accepted from all disciplines provided they meet selection criteria. Applicants must demonstrate access to institutional resources and infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum research effort commitment (percent effort)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are expected to commit a minimum of 80% of their time to conducting research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Investigator must commit at least 80% of full-time professional effort to research activities for the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application limit per applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may apply no more than two times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should track prior submissions; this is a hard limit on number of applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence and institutional guarantee
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must demonstrate that they are conducting the proposed research independently and the department must guarantee the Investigator is conducting the proposed research independently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence of dedicated laboratory space and institutional support is required for certain eligible categories (e.g., clinical instructors, distinguished fellows).

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent funding restriction at application
rubrics_metrics.description: Since the goal is to fund projects lacking sufficient preliminary data to secure traditional funding, the applicant should not have funding for this proposed project at time of application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While applicants should not already have funding for the proposed project, awardees are encouraged to seek additional funding during the award period to expand their projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission method and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply, applicants must log into Altum | Proposal Central and search for Damon Runyon-Rachleff Innovation Award. Applications are due by 4:00 pm Eastern Time on July 1, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application instructions are on the Damon Runyon Application Guidelines webpage and forms are within Proposal Central. No budget is required at the time of application.

rubrics_metrics.name: No preliminary budget required at application
rubrics_metrics.description: No budget is required at the time of application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are not required to submit a detailed budget with the application; however a budget is required at the beginning of each award year if funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award amount, duration, and continuation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 1 award: two years, $200,000 per year ($400,000 total) with opportunity for up to two additional years (up to four years total, $800,000) for select Innovators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support for years three and four is granted to those who demonstrate most significant progress; recipients present progress in person near end of second year and the committee will decide regarding continued funding. Awards are paid in increments of $200,000 per year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on indirect costs / institutional overhead
rubrics_metrics.description: The Award cannot be used for indirect costs or institutional overhead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award monies are direct research costs only and institutions may not charge overhead to these funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted uses of funds (flexibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovation Award funds may be used for Investigator salary, salaries for professional and technical personnel, special equipment, supplies and other miscellaneous items required to conduct the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funds are intended to be flexible and should be budgeted realistically and itemized by category according to the budget form instructions when submitted at the start of each award year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual budgeting and financial reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: All Awardees must submit projected annual budgets and yearly financial reports; awards are paid in increments of $200,000 per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the beginning of each award year a budget is required and submitted budgets should be realistic estimates itemized by category. Awardees must submit yearly financial reports (expenditure reports).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific annual progress report contents and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual progress reports: signed, due on the 15th day of the final month of each year of funding; must include a technical summary (≤4 pages), one-paragraph lay summary, collaborations description, outreach participation, updated NIH biosketch with bibliography, current and pending funding, list of conferences/presentations, changes in responsibilities/title, brief comments on most important accomplishment and obstacles, description of research and office space allocation, budget for next year, and completed Intellectual Property Disclosure Form; oral progress presentation in fall of second year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical summaries should be targeted to a general scientific audience and sufficiently detailed to describe activities; figures and references allowed if appropriate. Reports are kept strictly confidential and serve auditing, program evaluation, and publicity needs. If research differs from funded proposal, provide explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final progress report contents and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Final progress report: signed, should not exceed four pages, must include technical summary of research over award, one-paragraph lay summary detailing accomplishments and impact, collaborations description, outreach participation, updated NIH biosketch and bibliography, current/pending funding, list of presentations, changes in responsibilities/title, statement indicating how the award made a difference in the Investigator’s career, brief comments on most important accomplishment and obstacles, completed Intellectual Property Disclosure Form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final report mirrors annual report but focuses on overall accomplishments and career impact; include explanations for deviations from original proposal and supply reprints of publications from award period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sharing planning questions (reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators must report plans to share data (before or after publication) including type of data, where it will be shared (e.g., Figshare, Dataverse, OSF), who will prepare it, and expected costs of preparing/sharing data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include specifics about data type (genome/exome sequence, images, structures, software/algorithms), repository, responsible person, and cost estimates in annual and final reports as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property and invention reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees must adhere to the Foundation's invention policy and submit a completed Intellectual Property Disclosure Form with reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All awardees must follow the Foundation's invention policy (no individualized modifications) and submit disclosure forms as required; failure to comply with award terms may jeopardize award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and presentation acknowledgment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications (including abstracts) resulting from funded projects must acknowledge Damon Runyon-Rachleff Innovation Award support with a specified statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the exact acknowledgment: “[Name of Awardee] is a Damon Runyon-Rachleff Innovation Awardee supported (in part) by the Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation (DRR-#[___]).” Awardees are strongly encouraged to identify themselves as awardees when presenting or accepting honors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms regarding award assignment and employer relationship
rubrics_metrics.description: All awards are made to the sponsoring institution for support of the designated Innovator; an award does not create an employer-employee relationship between the Foundation and the awardee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions receive the award and must manage funds per Foundation policies; Foundation will not negotiate policy modifications with individual institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to seek Foundation approval for major changes
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Investigator wishes to discontinue the project, leave the designated institution, or modify any award agreement, they must seek approval from the Foundation in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to obtain prior approval may result in immediate termination of the Award and could jeopardize future awards to the institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review process oversight and decision authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards are approved by the Board of Directors acting upon recommendation of the Innovation Award Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee conducts reviews and makes recommendations; final approval rests with the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer unconscious bias awareness statement
rubrics_metrics.description: At the start of each review session reviewers are read a statement about the Foundation's commitment to excellence and diversity and to be aware of potential unconscious biases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is guidance to reviewers to acknowledge and mitigate unconscious bias when reviewing, scoring and discussing candidates and applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms and administrative documentation for awardees
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees must complete and submit various forms (Award Statement, Award Acceptance Form - Stage 1 and Stage 2, Budget Form, Expenditure Report Form, Invention Policy, Intellectual Property Disclosure Form, Cover Sheet Stage 2, Co-Applicant Cover Sheet Stage 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms are provided to awardees and must be completed according to instructions; these are required for acceptance, budgeting, reporting, and Stage 2 continuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility to provide publicity-relevant items
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should inform Award Programs when parts of their research are appropriate to highlight (fundamental advance, clinical trial development, patient-related anecdote, publications) for Foundation media outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports may be used by Foundation for public-facing materials; investigators are encouraged to contact Award Programs with items to share.
